A consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the top [[small forward]] in the 2021 class, he chose to forgo his [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|college eligibility]] and [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] to the 2020 class to join the [[NBA G League Ignite]]. Kuminga finished his high school career at [[The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]]. The [[Golden State Warriors]] selected Kuminga with the seventh overall pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]]. During his rookie season, he won an [[NBA champion]]ship with them in [[2021–22 Golden State Warriors season|2022]]. ==Early life== Kuminga began playing basketball in the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] at age two.{{cite web |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2019/07/13/jonathan-kuminga-makes-case-for-no-1-high-school-player-in-the-nation-talks-future-plans/ |title=Jonathan Kuminga makes case for No. 1 high school player in the nation, talks future plans |first=Adam |last=Zagoria |work=ZagsBlog |date=July 13, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2019}} In 2016, at 14 years old, he moved to the U.S. to play high school basketball.{{cite magazine |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=SI All-American TV: Top 2021 F Jonathan Kuminga Speaks on Social Injustice In Democratic Republic of Congo |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jonathan-kuminga-social-injustice-2021-duke-kentucky-auburn-texas-tech |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=July 16, 2020 |date=July 7, 2020}} ==High school career== As a freshman, Kuminga played basketball for [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]].{{cite web |last=Burlison |first=Frank |title=Two elite 2022 guards among Pangos East standouts |url=https://www.burlisononbasketball.com/2018/10/two-elite-2022-guards-among-pangos-east-standouts/ |publisher=Burlison on Basketball |access-date=August 14, 2019 |date=October 28, 2018}} For his sophomore season, he transferred to Our Savior New American School in [[Centereach, New York]] and averaged 25 points, five rebounds, and five assists per game.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2018–19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/wCRc7AkDlUOzrgbdS9nvZA/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=August 14, 2019 |date=April 18, 2019}} In January 2019, Kuminga was named [[most valuable player]] of the Slam Dunk to the Beach showcase after scoring 40 points, a single-game record at the event, in a loss to [[Gonzaga College High School]].{{cite web |last=Riedel |first=Kenny |title=Slam Dunk superlatives |url=https://www.capegazette.com/article/slam-dunk-superlatives/172369 |website=[[Cape Gazette]] |access-date=August 14, 2019 |date=January 2, 2019}} He earned [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards#Sophomore of the Year|MaxPreps National Sophomore of the Year]] honors. After the season, Kuminga averaged 20.8 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists per game for the NY Rens at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]], facing many players older than him. He scored 43 points, shooting 7 of 11 from three-point range, against the Texas Titans, a team featuring top recruits [[Cade Cunningham]] and [[Greg Brown III|Greg Brown]].{{cite web |url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article231895998.html |title=UK basketball scholarship offer led to (very) long-distance phone call for top recruit |first=Ben |last=Roberts |work=Kentucky.com |date=June 25, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190629055013/https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article231895998.html |archive-date=June 29, 2019 |url-status=live}} For his junior season, Kuminga transferred to [[The Patrick School]] in [[Hillside, New Jersey]].{{cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |title=No. 1 Chosen 25 junior Jonathan Kuminga transfers to The Patrick School |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2019/jonathan-kuminga-transfers-to-the-patrick-school |publisher=USA Today High School Sports |access-date=May 19, 2020 |date=August 26, 2017}} On December 23, 2019, he made his season debut, scoring 20 points in a win over [[Roselle Catholic High School]], after having been ruled ineligible for 30 days by the [[New Jersey State Interscholastic Athletic Association]] due to transfer rules.{{cite web |last=Zagoria |first=Adam |title=Jonathan Kuminga scores 20 in Patrick School debut after judge grants stay |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2019/12/23/jonathan-kuminga-is-now-immediately-eligible-at-the-patrick-school-after-judge-grants-stay/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=May 19, 2020 |date=December 23, 2019}} On January 3, 2020, Kuminga suffered an ankle sprain that sidelined him for about a month.{{cite web |last=Corrigan |first=James |title=Jonathan Kuminga returns from ankle injury, discusses Kobe's impact on his life |url=https://www.zagsblog.com/2020/02/05/jonathan-kuminga-returns-from-ankle-injury-discusses-kobes-impact-on-his-life/ |publisher=Zagsblog |access-date=May 19, 2020 |date=February 5, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 16.2 points, 5.5 rebounds and 3.7 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Greco |first1=Richard |last2=Kinney |first2=Mike |last3=Minnick |first3=Kevin |title=Boys Basketball: Second team All-State, 2019–2020 |url=https://www.nj.com/highschoolsports/2020/03/boys-basketball-second-team-all-state-2019-2020.html |publisher=[[NJ.com]] |access-date=May 19, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== As a high school sophomore, Kuminga emerged as one of the best [[college recruiting|recruits]] in the 2021 class, with most recruiting services ranking him first in his class by the time he was a junior.{{cite web |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Hoophall-Jonathan-Kuminga-shows-progression-as-high-majors-pursue-128074717/ |title=Hoophall: Jonathan Kuminga progresses, as high majors pursue |first=Evan |last=Daniels |work=[[247Sports.com]] |date=January 20, 2019 |access-date=August 11, 2019}} On July 15, 2020, he [[reclassification (education)|reclassified]] to the 2020 class and announced that he would bypass [[college basketball]] to join the [[NBA G League Ignite]] over offers from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], among other college programs.{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |title=Top-five prospect Jonathan Kuminga latest to bypass college for G League |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29470941 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 16, 2020 |date=July 15, 2020}} At the end of his high school career, he was a consensus five-star recruit and the best [[small forward]] in the 2020 class. He was considered the third-best player in his class by [[Rivals.com]] and the fourth best by [[247Sports.com]] and [[ESPN]] after reclassifying.{{cite web |title=Jonathan Kuminga, 2020 Small forward |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2021/jonathan-kuminga-208382 |publisher=[[Rivals.com]] |access-date=July 16, 2020}}{{cite web |title=Jonathan Kuminga – Basketball Recruiting – Player yes }} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2020–2021)=== On July 15, 2020, Kuminga signed a one-year contract with the [[NBA G League Ignite]], a developmental team affiliated with the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |date=July 16, 2020 |title=Five-Star Recruit Jonathan Kuminga Signs With NBA G League |url=https://pr.nba.com/five-star-recruit-jonathan-kuminga-signs-with-nba-g-league |access-date=April 14, 2023 |website=nba.com |publisher=}} On February 10, 2021, he made his debut, recording 19 points, four assists and four rebounds in a 110–104 win over the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |title=Jonathan Kuminga and Jalen Green: How did 2021 NBA Draft prospects play in their G League Ignite debut? |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/jonathan-kuminga-jalen-green-how-did-2021-nba-draft-prospects-play-in-their-g-league-ignite-debut-santa-cruz-warriors/12b0us3movepa13j1js64rb178 |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |access-date=April 23, 2021 |date=February 11, 2021}} Kuminga averaged 15.8 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.7 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |title=2021 NBA Draft: Jonathan Kuminga scouting report, strengths, weaknesses and player comparisons |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/ca/nba/news/2021-nba-draft-jonathan-kuminga-g-league-ignite-scouting-report-strengths-weaknesses-and-player-comparisons/11dsklbxfsdaw1v9u31g1umb4t |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]] |date=July 7, 2021 |access-date=April 14, 2023}} ===Golden State Warriors (2021–2026)=== The [[Golden State Warriors]] drafted Kuminga as the 7th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{cite news |last=Kurtenbach |first=Dieter |title=Kurtenbach: With Kuminga selection, the Warriors bet big on themselves |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2021/07/29/kurtenbach-in-kuminga-selection-the-warriors-organization-went-all-in-on-itself/ |access-date=July 30, 2021 |work=[[The Mercury News]] |date=July 30, 2021}} On August 3, 2021, he signed with the Warriors.{{cite web |title=Warriors Sign Jonathan Kuminga and Moses Moody |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-kuminga-moody-20210805 |website=nba.com |date=August 4, 2021 |access-date=August 6, 2021}} On October 30, Kuminga made his NBA debut, putting up three points and one steal in a 103–82 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/warriors-jonathan-kuminga-hits-3-pointer-nba-debut-gets-game-ball|title=Kuminga hits 3-pointer in Warriors debut, gets game ball|last=Thanawalla|first=Ali|website=NBC Sports|date=October 30, 2021|access-date=October 30, 2021}} On December 18, in his first career start, Kuminga put up a then career-high 26 points in a 119–100 loss to the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-jonathan-kuminga-gets-100-real-being-benched-games/|title=Warriors rookie Jonathan Kuminga gets 100% real on being benched games|website=ClutchPoints|last=Haynes|first=Mark|date=December 18, 2021|access-date=January 22, 2022}} On February 18, 2022, Kuminga participated in the [[Rising Stars Challenge]] game for the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]] weekend, replacing the injured [[Chris Duarte (basketball)|Chris Duarte]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/jonathan-kuminga-added-nba-rising-stars-game-replaces-chris-duarte|title=Kuminga added to Rising Stars Game at NBA All-Star Weekend|website=RSN|date=February 16, 2022 }}{{cite web | last=Shapiro | first=Michael | title=Jonathan Kuminga Could Be the Future of the Warriors | website=SI.com | date=2022-02-18 | url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/02/18/jonathan-kuminga-golden-state-warriors-rookie | access-date=2024-10-16}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Jonathan-Kuminga-underwhelmed-at-Rising-Stars-16931658.php|title=Jonathan Kuminga underwhelmed at Rising Stars, but his presence was all that mattered|first=Connor|last=Letourneau|date=February 19, 2022|website=San Francisco Chronicle}} Kuminga ended his rookie season as an [[NBA champion]] after the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in the [[2022 NBA Finals]].{{cite web|url=https://www.montereyherald.com/2022/06/18/warriors-will-jonathan-kuminga-play-in-summer-league/|title=Warriors: Will Jonathan Kuminga play in Summer League?|website=montereyherald.com|last=Kenney|first=Madeline|date=June 18, 2022|access-date=June 19, 2022}} At 19 years and 253 days, he became the second-youngest NBA champion, behind [[Darko Miličić]].{{Cite web |date=2022-06-17 |title=The youngest players to win an NBA title |url=https://hoopshype.com/gallery/youngest-players-nba-title-champions/ |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}} On January 24, 2024, Kuminga scored 25 points on a perfect 11-for-11 from the field in a victory against the [[Atlanta Hawks]]. This performance tied [[Chris Mullin]]'s Warriors franchise record for the most made shots in a game without a miss.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/observations-jonathan-kuminga-hawks-emotional/1695263/|title=What we learned as Kuminga takes flight in Warriors' emotional win|website=NBCsportsbayarea.com|last=Wagaman|first=Michael|date=January 24, 2024|access-date=January 25, 2024}} On December 27, 2024, Kuminga put up a career-high 34 points, along with 10 rebounds and five assists, in a 102–92 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/gameday-recap-20241227|title=Jonathan Kuminga Scores 34 Points and Leads Furious Comeback Effort in Loss to Clippers|website=nba.com|last=Champion|first=Kalyb|date=December 27, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}} On December 28, Kuminga put up a career-high-tying 34 points in a 109–105 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/warriors-news-jonathan-kuminga-makes-nervous-admission-playing-hero-suns|title=Warriors' Jonathan Kuminga makes 'nervous' admission after playing hero vs. Suns|website=ClutchPoints|last=Pavon|first=Josue|date=December 29, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}} On January 4, 2025, Kuminga suffered a [[sprained ankle]] in a 121–113 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{Cite web |date=2025-01-05 |title=Warriors' Kuminga (ankle) out at least 3 weeks |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/43301296/warriors-kuminga-least-3-weeks-ankle-sprain |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He then missed 31 consecutive games before returning to action on March 13 in a 130–104 win against the [[Sacramento Kings]], notching 18 points in just 20 minutes of action.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |last2=Youngmisuk |first2=Ohm |date=2025-03-11 |title=Sources: Kuminga (ankle) plans to return Thu. |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/44210450/warriors-jonathan-kuminga-ankle-plans-return-thursday-sources-say |access-date=2025-03-16 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} After a prolonged [[Restricted free agent (NBA)|restricted free agency]], which prevented the Warriors from making other signings, Kuminga signed a two-year, $48.5 million extension with the team on September 30, 2025.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-10-01 |title=Kuminga, Warriors end stalemate with 2-year deal |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46441474/warriors-jonathan-kuminga-agree-2-year-485-million-deal |access-date=2025-10-01 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2025-09-30 |title=Warriors Re-Sign Forward Jonathan Kuminga |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-re-sign-forward-jonathan-kuminga-20250930 |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} During a preseason game against the [[2025–26 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]], Kuminga was assessed a [[technical foul]] and ejected after arguing with referee [[Rodney Mott]], believing he was fouled on a drive to the rim. He was later fined $35,000 by the NBA for the incident.{{Cite web |last=Friedell |first=Nick |date=October 16, 2025 |title=Warriors’ Jonathan Kuminga fined $35,000 for illegal contact with official |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6723380/2025/10/16/warriors-jonathan-kuminga-fined-illegal-contact-official/ |access-date=October 16, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]]}} Kuminga made 20 appearances (including 13 starts) for the Warriors during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 12.1 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 2.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Jonathan Kuminga 2025-26 Stats per Game|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/4433247/jonathan-kuminga|access-date=April 4, 2026|website=espn.com|language=en}} ===Atlanta Hawks (2026)=== On February 5, 2026, Kuminga and [[Buddy Hield]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Kristaps Porziņģis]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-buddy-hield-and-jonathan-kuminga-from-golden-state|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Buddy Hield and Jonathan Kuminga from Golden State |work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2026}} On February 24, Kuminga made his debut for the Hawks, scoring 27 points on 9-of-12 shooting and adding seven rebounds, four assists, and two steals in 24 minutes off the bench in a 119–98 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/jonathan-kuminga-hawks-debut|title=Former Warrior Jonathan Kuminga makes his debut for the Atlanta Hawks |work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2026}} He also became the first player in Hawks franchise history to put up 25+ points in less than 30 minutes played in a debut.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-what-led-jonathan-kuminga-historic-debut-atlanta|title=What led to Jonathan Kuminga’s historic debut with Hawks|website=ClutchPoints|last=Brown|first=Malik|date=February 25, 2026|access-date=February 27, 2026}} On March 18, Kuminga hit an accidental full court shot in a 135-120 win over the Dallas Mavericks.https://clutchpoints.com/nba/atlanta-hawks/hawks-news-jonathan-kuminga-accidental-full-court-shot The Hawks faced the [[New York Knicks]] during their first-round playoff series. On April 18, Kuminga made his playoff debut for the Hawks, recording eight points and four rebounds in a 113–102 Game 1 loss.{{Cite web |title=BRUNSON AND TOWNS LEAD THE KNICKS PAST THE HAWKS 113-102 IN GAME 1 OF THEIR SERIES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500121 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} On April 23, he put up 21 points, four rebounds, and a block in a 109–108 Game 3 win, which gave the Hawks a 2–1 series lead.{{Cite web |title=MCCOLLUM RUINS KNICKS' NIGHT AGAIN, LEADING THE HAWKS TO A 109-108 VICTORY AND A 2-1 LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042500123 |access-date=May 1, 2026 |website=NBA.com}} The Hawks would go on to lose the series in six games. He became a [[Free agent (NBA)|free agent]] after Atlanta declined his $24.3 million team option.{{cite news|first= Anthony|last=Slater|title=Lakers land center Looney; in pursuit of Kuminga, sources say|date=July 7, 2026|work=ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49298644/sources-lakers-continue-pursuit-free-agent-jonathan-kuminga|access-date=July 7, 2026}} ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2026–present)=== On September 4, 2026, Kuminga signed a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves.{{Cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Jonathan Kuminga|website=NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-jonathan-kuminga|date=September 4, 2026}}{{Cite web|title=Jonathan Kuminga reaches 2-year, $12.4M deal with Timberwolves|website=espn.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49736014/jonathan-kuminga-reaches-2-year-deal-minnesota-timberwolves|date=August 26, 2026}} == National team career == In August 2022, Kuminga joined the [[DR Congo men's national basketball team]] for the African [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Africa)|2023 World Cup qualifiers]].{{Cite web |title=Splash brothers, Ibaka, Iggy encouraged me to play for my national team - Kuminga |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/african-qualifiers/news/splash-brothers-ibaka-iggy-encouraged-me-to-play-for-my-national-team-kuminga |access-date=2022-08-27 |website=FIBA.basketball |date=August 25, 2022 |language=en}} His older brother, Joel Ntambwe, was also on the roster. On August 26, 2022, he scored a team-high 18 points along with 6 rebounds for Congo in a 69–71 loss to [[Cameroon men's national basketball team|Cameroon]].{{Cite web |title=Congo DR v Cameroon boxscore - FIBA Basketball World Cup 2023 African Qualifiers - 26 August |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/african-qualifiers/game/2608/Congo-DR-Cameroon |access-date=2022-08-27
